title: Knee: cartilage, osteochondral lesions, and synovium
source: Core Radiology, 2nd edition, section 13.13 Knee, chunk 3

items.title: Osgood-Schlatter: edema pattern
items.alt: Sagittal fluid-sensitive MRI showing fragmentation and edema at the tibial tubercle
items.see: The tibial tubercle is enlarged and fragmented, with edema around the distal patellar tendon and in Hoffa fat pad.
items.why: The edema pattern connects repetitive traction injury to the symptomatic tibial tubercle in an adolescent.

items.title: Osgood-Schlatter: tubercle fragmentation
items.alt: Sagittal proton-density MRI showing an enlarged fragmented tibial tubercle
items.see: The fragmented tibial tubercle lies at the distal patellar-tendon attachment.
items.why: The structural view complements the fluid-sensitive image and localizes the osteochondrosis.

items.title: Superficial versus deep cartilage fissuring
items.alt: Axial MRI showing superficial and deep trochlear cartilage fissures
items.see: The yellow arrow marks superficial fissuring; the red arrow marks a deeper defect extending beyond half the cartilage thickness.
items.why: Depth separates Outerbridge grade 2 from grade 3 injury.

items.title: Full-thickness cartilage defect
items.alt: Axial MRI showing a full-thickness medial patellar cartilage defect with delamination
items.see: The defect traverses the entire cartilage thickness and delaminates toward the median ridge.
items.why: Full-thickness loss is Outerbridge grade 4 disease.

items.title: Outerbridge cartilage grading
items.alt: Table comparing grades zero through four of cartilage degeneration
items.see: Progression runs from normal cartilage to heterogeneous signal, superficial fissuring, deep fissuring, and full-thickness loss.
items.why: The table provides a compact visual scaffold, although descriptive reporting remains preferred.

items.title: Acute osteochondral fracture
items.alt: Axial fluid-sensitive MRI showing a displaced lateral trochlear osteochondral fracture
items.see: A displaced fragment includes articular cartilage, the subchondral plate, and subchondral bone.
items.why: Acute traumatic osteochondral injury is especially important in a younger patient.

items.title: Subchondral insufficiency fracture
items.alt: Coronal MRI showing irregular thickening of the subchondral bone plate with surrounding edema
items.see: The subchondral plate is thickened and irregular with exuberant adjacent marrow edema.
items.why: In a middle-aged or older patient, this pattern favors subchondral insufficiency fracture.

items.title: Unstable osteochondral lesion with AVN
items.alt: Coronal MRI showing fluid undercutting an osteochondral lesion and serpiginous marrow abnormality
items.see: Fluid undercuts the subchondral plate while a separate serpiginous marrow pattern supports avascular necrosis.
items.why: Deep fluid or cystic change signals instability and potential displacement.

items.title: Arthroscopic confirmation of instability
items.alt: Arthroscopic photograph showing a probe elevating an unstable osteochondral defect
items.see: The probe can elevate the osteochondral fragment from its bed.
items.why: This is the operative correlate of fluid undercutting the lesion on MRI.

items.title: PVNS on radiography
items.alt: Lateral knee radiograph showing a dense effusion and posterior soft-tissue mass
items.see: There is a dense joint effusion and a lobulated soft-tissue mass posterior to the knee.
items.why: Radiography may suggest the synovial process even though MRI characterizes it better.

items.title: PVNS low-signal masses
items.alt: Axial proton-density MRI showing low-signal masses posterior to the knee
items.see: Multiple low-signal synovial masses occupy the posterior knee.
items.why: Hemosiderin from recurrent hemorrhage produces characteristically dark signal.

items.title: PVNS blooming on gradient echo
items.alt: Sagittal gradient-echo MRI showing markedly dark blooming synovial masses
items.see: The masses become extremely dark and conspicuous on the susceptibility-sensitive sequence.
items.why: Blooming is the imaging consequence of paramagnetic hemosiderin.

items.title: PVNS at arthroscopy
items.alt: Arthroscopic photograph showing multiple brown synovial-based masses
items.see: Nodular brown synovial masses fill the joint space.
items.why: The gross appearance reflects hemosiderin-laden hyperplastic synovium.

items.title: Lipoma arborescens without fat suppression
items.alt: Coronal MRI without fat suppression showing frond-like fatty synovial proliferation
items.see: Globular and frond-like synovial tissue follows bright fat signal.
items.why: Recognizing the fatty architecture distinguishes lipoma arborescens from hemosiderin-rich PVNS.

items.title: Lipoma arborescens with fat suppression
items.alt: Coronal fat-suppressed MRI showing suppression of frond-like synovial tissue
items.see: The frond-like tissue suppresses with fat, confirming its fatty composition.
items.why: Signal suppression is the paired-sequence proof that the synovial proliferation contains fat.

items.title: Lipoma arborescens: axial distribution
items.alt: Axial fat-suppressed MRI showing lobulated fatty synovial proliferation around the patellofemoral joint
items.see: Lobulated fronds occupy the joint recesses around the patellofemoral compartment.
items.why: The axial view shows the extent and intracapsular distribution of the process.
